rationale: The Latin anchors *sonus* (sound/noise) and *impressio* (a striking/blow), alongside *contusio* (a bruise/blow), point to a sense of a loud impact noise rather than a vehicular accident or financial collapse. Among the candidates, clang.n.01 ("a loud resonant repeating noise") best captures the auditory/percussive quality implied by *sonus*, while also being compatible with the physical striking sense of *contusio*/*impressio*; the vehicular or financial crash senses (crash.n.02, .n.03) are anachronistic and contextually inappropriate for Old English usage.
